text: Designing a good REST API is like building a clear road map for other developers. First, keep your endpoints simple and consistent. For example, use nouns like `/users` or `/orders` instead of verbs such as `/getUser`. Always use proper HTTP status codes to tell clients what happened: `200` for success, `404` for not found, and `400` for bad requests. Next, never forget versioning. Start with `/v1/` in your URL so you can add new features later without breaking existing users. Finally, write clear documentation. List each endpoint, its parameters, and example responses. Good docs save hours of confusion. Follow these rules, and your API will be easy to use and maintain.
